title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a complex manifold and Y a closed complex submanifold of pure codimension p. The holomorphic de Rham complex Ω•_X resolves the constant sheaf C. The page compares two local fundamental classes of Y, both living in the local-cohomology sheaf H^{2p}_Y.

(1) The topological class. Local Poincaré/Thom duality gives an isomorphism Z_Y ≅ H^{2p}_Y(X,Z), and similarly over C (written P^Z_top and P^C_top). The image of 1 is the local orientation (Thom) class of the normal bundle.

(2) The analytic class. Grothendieck defines it 'by algebraic means', which he says matches the algebraic class. If f_1,…,f_p are local equations of Y, take the symbol df_1/f_1 ∧ … ∧ df_p/f_p. This is a section of the local cohomology sheaf H^p_Y(Ω^p_X), represented by a Čech cocycle on the complement of Y. It is then pushed into H^{2p}_Y(X,Ω•_X) by the edge map of the Hodge-filtration spectral sequence. This gives P^C_an : C_Y → H^{2p}_Y(Ω•_X), which he labels 'résidu' and 'Poincaré analytique local'.

(3) The comparison chain. H^{2p}_Y(X,Z) → H^{2p}_Y(X,Z)⊗C ≅ H^{2p}_Y(X,C) ≅ H^{2p}_Y(X,Ω•_X), the last step being the de Rham isomorphism. The claim is that the square closes up with the factor 1/(2πi)^p on C_Y: the analytic class equals (2πi)^p times the image of the topological class.

Proof strategy:
- Reduce to the case where Y is a point a, by taking a transversal slice X' of dimension n−p that meets Y in a point.
- Then reduce, via cup/exterior products (X locally a product of discs, the class a product of the dz_i/z_i), to dim X = 1.
- His N.B.: this product principle mainly shows the comparison constant has the form λ^p, with λ ∈ C* independent of X, Y and p.

The case dim X = 1, X a disc around a. The coboundary isomorphisms H^1(X−a, ·) ≅ H^2_a(X, ·) relate everything to the punctured disc. The analytic class is dz/z in H^1_a(X,Ω^1). Its de Rham image in H^1(X−a,C) pairs with the positively oriented loop to give ∮dz/z = 2πi, while the integral generator pairs to 1. Hence λ = 2πi, up to sign conventions.

The drawing of a circle around a point is the linking loop. This is the transcendental comparison serving the previous page's 'Hodge functors on motives': the comparison of fiber functors / realizations and the Tate twist Z(p) = (2πi)^p Z.
errors: No real mathematical error. The constant is correctly 2πi in dimension 1, giving (2πi)^p in codimension p.

Sign conventions are left implicit: the orientation of C, the sign of the coboundary H^1(X−a) → H^2_a, and the Koszul signs in the cup-product reduction (possibly (−1)^{p(p−1)/2}). These could make λ = ±2πi or add a sign in general. He hedges by proving only 'a multiplier of the form λ^p'.
The reduction to a transversal slice uses functoriality of both local classes under restriction to a transversal submanifold. This is standard but not argued on the page.

ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's local fundamental class / residue symbol; cycle class in Hodge/de Rham cohomology with supports
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (residue symbol, Hartshorne's Residues and Duality, 1966); systematized by El Zein (1978) and Deligne (SGA 4½ 'Cycle')
ideas.where_published: Circulated through Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, and Grothendieck's de Rham cohomology paper (IHES 1966); exact form unsure

ideas.what: Comparison: analytic/de Rham cycle class = (2πi)^p × topological (Thom) class
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of de Rham and Betti cycle classes up to Tate twist (2πi)^p

ideas.where_published: Implicit in Grothendieck's 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966)

ideas.what: Reduction to the codim-1 point case via transversal slices and products, giving a universal constant λ^p, then computing λ = 2πi by the residue of dz/z
ideas.modern_name: Standard reduction to curves; residue theorem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard verification of the (2πi)^p normalization between algebraic/analytic and topological fundamental classes. It is well known (Deligne, El Zein) and serves as a routine lemma for the Hodge realization of motives.
transcription_corrections: The annotation next to the arrow from H^p_Y(X,Ω^p_X) is likely 'suite spectrale' (edge map of the spectral sequence), not 'point spécial'.
'Poincaré topologique local' labels the vertical isomorphism Z_Y → H^{2p}_Y(X,Z). The arrow Z_Y → C_Y is the coefficient extension.
The bottom line of the diagram is C_Y --1/(2iπ)^p--> C_Y, connecting the domains of P^C_top and P^C_an. The crossed-out item is a struck H^{2p}_Y(X,Ω•_X).
In the dim-1 diagram, the arrow into H^2_a(X,Ω•_X) is from H^1_a(X,Ω^1_X), with dz/z as the generating section.
